import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from doorstop import Doorstop, Requirement

class TestDoorstopRequirements(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self.doorstop = Doorstop()

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.store')
    def test_store_requirements(self, mock_store):
        # Test storing requirements
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        self.doorstop.store_requirement(requirement)
        mock_store.assert_called_once_with(requirement)

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.update')
    def test_handle_change_management(self, mock_update):
        # Test handling change management
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        updated_requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Updated Requirement', description='Updated description.')
        self.doorstop.update_requirement(requirement, updated_requirement)
        mock_update.assert_called_once_with(updated_requirement)

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.update')
    def test_associate_changes_with_developer(self, mock_update):
        # Test associating changes with developer
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        updated_requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Updated Requirement', description='Updated description.')
        developer_id = 'dev123'
        self.doorstop.update_requirement(requirement, updated_requirement, developer_id)
        mock_update.assert_called_once_with(updated_requirement, developer_id)

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.store')
    def test_scalability_with_large_number_of_requirements(self, mock_store):
        # Test scalability with large number of requirements
        requirements = [Requirement(id=f'REQ{i:03}', title=f'Requirement {i}', description=f'Description {i}') for i in range(1000)]
        for requirement in requirements:
            self.doorstop.store_requirement(requirement)
        self.assertEqual(mock_store.call_count, 1000)

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.install')
    def test_lightweight_installation(self, mock_install):
        # Test lightweight installation
        self.doorstop.install()
        mock_install.assert_called_once()

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.store')
    def test_store_requirements_failure(self, mock_store):
        # Test storing requirements failure
        mock_store.side_effect = Exception('Storage failure')
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as context:
            self.doorstop.store_requirement(requirement)
        self.assertEqual(str(context.exception), 'Storage failure')

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.update')
    def test_handle_change_management_failure(self, mock_update):
        # Test handling change management failure
        mock_update.side_effect = Exception('Update failure')
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        updated_requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Updated Requirement', description='Updated description.')
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as context:
            self.doorstop.update_requirement(requirement, updated_requirement)
        self.assertEqual(str(context.exception), 'Update failure')

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.update')
    def test_associate_changes_with_developer_failure(self, mock_update):
        # Test associating changes with developer failure
        mock_update.side_effect = Exception('Update failure')
        requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Sample Requirement', description='This is a sample requirement.')
        updated_requirement = Requirement(id='REQ001', title='Updated Requirement', description='Updated description.')
        developer_id = 'dev123'
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as context:
            self.doorstop.update_requirement(requirement, updated_requirement, developer_id)
        self.assertEqual(str(context.exception), 'Update failure')

    @patch('doorstop.storage.Storage.install')
    def test_lightweight_installation_failure(self, mock_install):
        # Test lightweight installation failure
        mock_install.side_effect = Exception('Installation failure')
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as context:
            self.doorstop.install()
        self.assertEqual(str(context.exception), 'Installation failure')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
